text: Thornton!” said Margaret, a little surprised. “I thought——” “Well, little one, what did you think?” asked Frederick, as she did not finish her sentence. “Oh, only,” said she, reddening and looking straight at him, “I fancied you meant some one of a different class, not a gentleman; somebody come on an errand.” “He looked like someone of that kind,” said Frederick, carelessly. “I took him for a shopman, and he turns out a manufacturer.” Margaret was silent. She remembered how at first, before she knew his character, she had spoken and thought of him just as Frederick was doing.
